svg.title: Orchestrate. Harness. Or be orchestrated.
svg.desc: Beto's argument for experienced professionals leading AI-assisted work: direct the work, check the result, keep human responsibility. His lived journey, three conditional future possibilities, and mAInCharacter advisory and AI setup booking options.
svg.text: Give AI clear jobs. Keep the work organized. Check what comes back.
Or someone else will decide how your expertise fits into their process.
AI Quotient (AIQ): how well you use AI, check its work and lead others doing the same.
YOU KNOW THE WORK. BECOME THE CONDUCTOR.
AI helps with the parts. You judge the whole.
AI makes answers easier to get. You still need to know which questions matter,
what good work looks like, and when an answer does not make sense.
More agents do not automatically mean better work.
Give each one a distinct job. Judge the result after checking and corrections.
What is fun, what is productive and what is monetizable are different.
Inside an organization, prove one useful improvement.
Get permission. Try one small piece of work. Have someone else check it.
Then discuss what the improvement changes for your role—not just your workload.
I DID NOT START WITH AGENTS. I STARTED WITH SPREADSHEETS.
I turned spreadsheets into tools. Then came Linear, repeatable skills, local models
in LM Studio, and now Orca to organize agent work. Each step meant learning—and rework.
My point: experience matters more when you can turn it into a way of working others can use.
More work continues while you are away.
Your agent may coordinate with theirs.
Who is allowed to make a commitment?
The risk: promises pile up before
people can understand or stop them.
But trust, permission, money and the physical world do not move at software speed.
mAInCharacter helps experienced professionals turn expertise into a clearer next move.
your value and the choices ahead.
Choose tools, set up, try real work.
